description: Wang and colleagues publish supplementary data for an SDG13.1.1 disaster assessment of 73 Belt and Road countries. Science Data Bank exposes a PUBLIC CC0 release with two files totalling 161.53 KB. Its description names calculation variables, disaster types by country, and calculated values and trends for deaths, missing people and people directly affected per 100,000 population. An infrastructure modeller could use these country-level outcomes to provide historical disaster context or to compare broad regional exposure assumptions. The indicators are outcomes across people and disasters, not direct measures of asset damage, service interruption or local vulnerability. They derive from EM-DAT and the paper’s calculations, so input coverage and definitions constrain their interpretation. The provider page does not identify the exact years or file formats in the inspected metadata. The files were not downloaded to inspect columns or distinguish annual values from aggregate trends. Local emergency-service or network simulations would need event locations, assets and finer population data before these indicators could calibrate mechanisms. Related event, population and infrastructure records are needed to test local service impacts.
